slides.headline: They wanted to reach heaven. Look at the foundations.
slides.sub: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Tower of Babel, 1563

slides.headline: The plan
slides.text: In the Bible, people decide to build a tower that reaches the sky. Bruegel shows it halfway built, and already in trouble.

slides.headline: The king
slides.text: In the front, the king comes to inspect his tower. The stonemasons kneel before him in the dust and rubble.

slides.headline: The tower
slides.text: The tower spirals up like a giant cake. Its arches recall the Colosseum in Rome, which Bruegel had seen with his own eyes.

slides.headline: The flaw
slides.text: Look closely at the layers: the arches don't line up and the floors already tilt. It is going wrong from the bottom.

slides.headline: The workers
slides.text: Hundreds of tiny workers swarm everywhere, with cranes, ladders and ropes. Bruegel painted each one busy at a job.

slides.headline: The city
slides.text: Around the tower, a whole city carries on as usual, and ships crowd the harbour, bringing in more stone.

slides.headline: The ending
slides.text: In the story, God confuses their language so they cannot understand each other. The work stops, unfinished forever.

slides.headline: Too ambitious?
slides.text: A dream so big it sinks under its own weight. Would you keep building, or stop before it is too late?
